Parametric Skills: Test Fixture

This is a small mock paper used by tests/test_paper_retrieval_core.py. It
mirrors the section structure of arXiv 2606.30015 (ParametricSkills) with
the relevant pieces trimmed. Lines are LF-separated, blank-line-delimited
paragraphs, so the segmenter can split into blocks.

Abstract

ParametricSkills converts textual skills into LoRA adapters via a
hypernetwork. It outperforms in-context learning by 6.44 points on SWE
benchmarks. The hypernetwork is trained in two stages: Skill-Reconstruction
Pretraining and Exploitation Post-Training.

1 Introduction

Agentic LLMs struggle to faithfully follow long skill instructions. We
argue that parameterising skills as LoRA adapters makes them more robust.

2 Related Work

Prior work explores prompt-based skill retrieval. Our contribution is
parameterising skills directly into model weights.

3 Method

ParametricSkills has two training stages. Stage one teaches the
hypernetwork to reconstruct a skill's content from its text. Stage two
trains the policy to exploit skills end-to-end.

3.1 Skill-Reconstruction Pretraining

Given a skill in natural language, the hypernetwork outputs LoRA matrices
A and B such that W + delta W produces an LLM that, when queried about
the skill, can answer correctly.

We optimise the reconstruction loss between the predicted skill content
and the ground-truth skill text, using a cross-entropy objective applied
to the frozen base LLM's output.

3.2 Exploitation Post-Training

We train the agent on trajectories where skills are injected via LoRA,
not via prompt. The reward signal comes from successful task completion
on SWE-bench tasks.

4 Experiments

ParametricSkills outperforms in-context learning on six SWE subtasks.
BERT-Score and F1 also improve, confirming the adapter is faithful to
the source skill.

5 Conclusion

Parameterising skills via a hypernetwork is a promising direction for
continual learning at inference time.
